Stream-Balls is a technique for visualizing steady-state vector fields that constructs a scalar potential field from advected particles or streamlines using blobby functions, then extracts iso-contours to mimic stream surfaces [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the description of 'Stream-Balls' provided in Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that Stream-Balls build a scalar function (potential field) from advected particles or streamlines using blobby functions (specifically Gaussian functions), sum them to create an analytical function, sample it on a grid, and take an iso-contour to produce surfaces that mimic stream surfaces.

**Formulas:** The potential field is constructed as $V(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{i} \sum_{t} \exp\left(-\frac{\|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{p}_{i,t}\|^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)$, where $\mathbf{p}_{i,t}$ is the position of particle $i$ at time $t$, and $\sigma$ controls the blobby spread [S1, unofficial].

The claim describes the construction of a potential field using a sum of Gaussian functions (blobby functions) over particles and time steps, which matches the description in Source [S1] ('placing a Gaussian function at each advected position... summing over all of the time steps... and summing over many different particles'). The mathematical formula provided in the claim is a standard representation of this process (sum of Gaussians), and the variable definitions ($p_{i,t}$ as position, $sigma$ as spread) are consistent with the concept of Gaussian blobby functions described in the text.
supported
